sanskrit: etena hi tadā rājaṃs tapa āsthāya dāruṇam sudurlabho varo labdhaḥ pāṇḍavān yoddhum āhave
english: For he it was, O king, who once undertook a fearsome austerity and won a boon most difficult to obtain — to fight the Pāṇḍavas in battle.

sanskrit: sa eṣa rathaśārdūlas tad vairaṃ saṃsmaran raṇe yotsyate pāṇḍavāṃs tāta prāṇāṃs tyaktvā sudustyajān
english: That tiger among chariot-warriors, remembering that enmity in battle, will fight the Pāṇḍavas, my son, casting aside his own life that is so hard to cast away.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sudakṣiṇas tu kāmbojo ratha ekaguṇo mataḥ tavārthasiddhim ākāṅkṣan yotsyate samare paraiḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja I reckon a chariot-warrior of single measure; desiring the fulfillment of your cause, he will fight the foe in battle.

sanskrit: etasya rathasiṃhasya tavārthe rājasattama parākramaṃ yathendrasya drakṣyanti kuravo yudhi
english: The valor of this lion among chariot-warriors, spent in your cause, O best of kings, the Kurus shall behold in the fray as though it were Indra's own.

sanskrit: etasya rathavaṃśo hi tigmavegaprahāriṇām kāmbojānāṃ mahārāja śalabhānām ivāyatiḥ
english: His ranks of chariots, O great king, manned by the Kāmbojas who strike with fierce and sudden speed, stretch on like a swarm of locusts.

sanskrit: nīlo māhiṣmatīvāsī nīlavarmadharas tava rathavaṃśena śatrūṇāṃ kadanaṃ vai kariṣyati
english: Nīla, dweller in Māhiṣmatī, clad in dark-blue armor, will work with his chariot ranks a great slaughter of your enemies.

sanskrit: kṛtavairaḥ purā caiva sahadevena pārthivaḥ yotsyate satataṃ rājaṃs tavārthe kurusattama
english: Having made enmity of old with Sahadeva, that prince will fight unceasingly in your cause, O king, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau sametau rathasattamau kṛtinau samare tāta dṛḍhavīryaparākramau
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, united, are foremost among chariot-warriors, accomplished in battle, my son, firm in might and valor.

sanskrit: etau tau puruṣavyāghrau ripusainyaṃ pradhakṣyataḥ gadāprāsāsinārācais tomaraiś ca bhujacyutaiḥ
english: These two tigers among men will consume the enemy host with mace and javelin, sword and iron shaft, and with lances hurled from their arms.

sanskrit: yuddhābhikāmau samare krīḍantāv iva yūthapau yūthamadhye mahārāja vicarantau kṛtāntavat
english: Eager for battle, sporting in the fray like two herd-leaders, they will range through the midst of the host, O great king, like Death itself.

sanskrit: trigartā bhrātaraḥ pañca rathodārā matā mama kṛtavairāś ca pārthena virāṭanagare tadā
english: The five Trigarta brothers I count exalted among chariot-warriors, who made their enmity with Pārtha then, in the city of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: makarā iva rājendra samuddhatataraṅgiṇīm gaṅgāṃ vikṣobhayiṣyanti pārthānāṃ yudhi vāhinīm
english: Like sea-monsters, O lord of kings, churning the Gaṅgā with her high-tossing waves, they will throw the army of the Pārthas into turmoil in the fight.

sanskrit: te rathāḥ pañca rājendra yeṣāṃ satyaratho mukham ete yotsyanti samare saṃsmarantaḥ purā kṛtam
english: These five are chariot-warriors, O lord of kings, with Satyaratha at their head; they will fight in battle, remembering what was done of old.

sanskrit: vyalīkaṃ pāṇḍaveyena bhīmasenānujena ha diśo vijayatā rājañ śvetavāhena bhārata
english: They remember the wrong done by the son of Pāṇḍu, the younger brother of Bhīmasena, who, conquering the quarters with his white-horsed car, O king, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: te haniṣyanti pārthānāṃ samāsādya mahārathān varān varān maheṣvāsān kṣatriyāṇāṃ dhuraṃdharāḥ
english: — closing in, these bearers of the warrior's burden will slay the great chariot-warriors of the Pārthas, the choicest of the mighty archers among the kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tava putras tu tathā duḥśāsanasya ca ubhau tau puruṣavyāghrau saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinau
english: Your son Lakṣmaṇa, and likewise the son of Duḥśāsana — both these tigers among men never turn back in battle.

sanskrit: taruṇau sukumārau ca rājaputrau tarasvinau yuddhānāṃ ca viśeṣajñau praṇetārau ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Young and tender, both these princes are swift and spirited, skilled in the particulars of war and leaders in every kind of it.

sanskrit: rathau tau rathaśārdūla matau me rathasattamau kṣatradharmaratau vīrau mahat karma kariṣyataḥ
english: These two chariot-warriors, O tiger among them, I reckon foremost; devoted to the kṣatriya's duty, those heroes will accomplish a mighty deed.

sanskrit: daṇḍadhāro mahārāja ratha eko nararṣabhaḥ yotsyate samaraṃ prāpya svena sainyena pālitaḥ
english: Daṇḍadhāra, O great king, is a chariot-warrior of single measure, a bull among men; reaching the battlefield, guarded by his own troops, he will fight.

sanskrit: bṛhadbalas tathā rājā kausalyo rathasattamaḥ ratho mama matas tāta dṛḍhavegaparākramaḥ
english: And King Bṛhadbala of Kosala, foremost among chariot-warriors, I count a true chariot-warrior, my son, firm in onset and valor.

sanskrit: eṣa yotsyati saṃgrāme svāṃ camūṃ saṃpraharṣayan ugrāyudho maheṣvāso dhārtarāṣṭrahite rataḥ
english: He will fight in the battle, rousing his own army to joy, a great archer wielding fearsome weapons, intent on the welfare of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: kṛpaḥ śāradvato rājan rathayūthapayūthapaḥ priyān prāṇān parityajya pradhakṣyati ripūṃs tava
english: Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, O king, is a leader among the leaders of chariot-bands; surrendering his own dear life, he will consume your foes.

sanskrit: gautamasya maharṣer ya ācāryasya śaradvataḥ kārttikeya ivājeyaḥ śarastambāt suto 'bhavat
english: He who was born from a clump of reeds, son of the great sage Gautama, the teacher Śaradvat — unconquerable like Kārttikeya.

sanskrit: eṣa senāṃ bahuvidhāṃ vividhāyudhakārmukām agnivat samare tāta cariṣyati vimardayan
english: He will range through the manifold host arrayed with diverse weapons and bows, my son, like fire in the battle, crushing it as he goes.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śakunir mātulas te 'sau ratha eko narādhipa prasajya pāṇḍavair vairaṃ yotsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Śakuni, your maternal uncle, O ruler of men, is a chariot-warrior of single measure; clinging to his enmity with the Pāṇḍavas, he will fight — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: etasya sainyā durdharṣāḥ samare 'pratiyāyinaḥ vikṛtāyudhabhūyiṣṭhā vāyuvegasamā jave
english: His soldiers are hard to assail, irresistible in battle, armed for the most part with strange weapons, in swiftness equal to the speed of the wind.

sanskrit: droṇaputro maheṣvāsaḥ sarveṣām ati dhanvinām samare citrayodhī ca dṛḍhāstraś ca mahārathaḥ
english: The son of Droṇa, a great archer above all bowmen, fights with cunning craft in battle, sure of aim, a mighty chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: etasya hi mahārāja yathā gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ śarāsanād vinirmuktāḥ saṃsaktā yānti sāyakāḥ
english: For his arrows, O great king, like those of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, loosed from the bow, fly forth in unbroken streams.

sanskrit: naiṣa śakyo mayā vīraḥ saṃkhyātuṃ rathasattamaḥ nirdahed api lokāṃs trīn icchann eṣa mahāyaśāḥ
english: This hero, foremost among chariot-warriors, I cannot fully reckon; this man of great renown could, if he wished, burn down the three worlds.

sanskrit: krodhas tejaś ca tapasā saṃbhṛto ''śramavāsinā droṇenānugṛhītaś ca divyair astrair udāradhīḥ
english: His wrath and fiery splendor were gathered through the austerity of the hermitage-dweller, and that noble-minded one was favored by Droṇa with celestial weapons.

sanskrit: doṣas tv asya mahān eko yenaiṣa bharatarṣabha na me ratho nātiratho mataḥ pārthivasattama
english: Yet one great fault he has, on whose account, O bull of the Bhāratas, I count him neither a chariot-warrior nor a great chariot-warrior, O best of kings.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ priyam atyartham āyuṣkāmaḥ sadā dvijaḥ na hy asya sadṛśaḥ kaś cid ubhayoḥ senayor api
english: Life is exceedingly dear to him; this brāhmaṇa ever longs to live. Yet none is his equal in either of the two armies.

sanskrit: hanyād ekarathenaiva devānām api vāhinīm vapuṣmāṃs talaghoṣeṇa sphoṭayed api parvatān
english: With a single chariot he could slay even the army of the gods, and that mighty-framed one could split mountains with the thunder of his palms.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyaguṇo vīraḥ prahartā dāruṇadyutiḥ daṇḍapāṇir ivāsahyaḥ kālavat pracariṣyati
english: A hero of countless qualities, a striker of terrible splendor, irresistible like Yama staff in hand, he will range the field like Death itself.

sanskrit: yugāntāgnisamaḥ krodhe siṃhagrīvo mahāmatiḥ eṣa bhārata yuddhasya pṛṣṭhaṃ saṃśamayiṣyati
english: In wrath like the fire at the world's end, lion-necked, of mighty mind — this man, O Bhārata, will bring the back of the war to its close.

sanskrit: pitā tv asya mahātejā vṛddho 'pi yuvabhir varaḥ raṇe karma mahat kartā tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: But his father, of great splendor, though aged is finer than the young; that he will do a mighty deed in battle, of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: astravegāniloddhūtaḥ senākakṣendhanotthitaḥ pāṇḍuputrasya sainyāni pradhakṣyati jaye dhṛtaḥ
english: Fanned by the wind of his weapons' speed, kindled by the host as by dry grass for fuel, he will burn up the armies of Pāṇḍu's son, fixed upon victory.

sanskrit: rathayūthapayūthānāṃ yūthapaḥ sa nararṣabhaḥ bhāradvājātmajaḥ kartā karma tīvraṃ hitāya vaḥ
english: That bull among men, leader of the bands of chariot-leaders, the son of Bharadvāja, will do a fierce deed for your benefit.

sanskrit: sarvamūrdhābhiṣiktānām ācāryaḥ sthaviro guruḥ gacched antaṃ sṛñjayānāṃ priyas tv asya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The teacher and aged preceptor of all the consecrated kings, he could bring the Sṛñjayas to their end — yet Dhanaṃjaya is dear to him.

sanskrit: naiṣa jātu maheṣvāsaḥ pārtham akliṣṭakāriṇam hanyād ācāryakaṃ dīptaṃ saṃsmṛtya guṇanirjitam
english: Never would this great archer slay Pārtha, the tireless doer, remembering his own blazing teaching and how it was conquered by Pārtha's virtues.

sanskrit: ślāghaty eṣa sadā vīraḥ pārthasya guṇavistaraiḥ putrād abhyadhikaṃ caiva bhāradvājo 'nupaśyati
english: This hero ever praises the abundance of Pārtha's virtues; the son of Bharadvāja looks upon him as more than a son.

sanskrit: hanyād ekarathenaiva devagandharvadānavān ekībhūtān api raṇe divyair astraiḥ pratāpavān
english: With a single chariot the mighty one could slay the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas, even were they joined as one in battle, with his celestial weapons.

sanskrit: pauravo rājaśārdūlas tava rājan mahārathaḥ mato mama ratho vīra paravīrarathārujaḥ
english: Paurava, that tiger among kings, O king, your great chariot-warrior, I count a true chariot-warrior, O hero — a breaker of the cars of enemy heroes.

sanskrit: svena sainyena sahitaḥ pratapañ śatruvāhinīm pradhakṣyati sa pāñcālān kakṣaṃ kṛṣṇagatir yathā
english: United with his own troops, scorching the enemy host, he will consume the Pāñcālas as fire whose path is black devours dry grass.

sanskrit: satyavrato rathavaro rājaputro mahārathaḥ tava rājan ripubale kālavat pracariṣyati
english: Satyavrata, foremost of chariot-warriors, a prince and a great chariot-warrior, will range through the enemy's host, O king, like Death itself.

sanskrit: etasya yodhā rājendra vicitrakavacāyudhāḥ vicariṣyanti saṃgrāme nighnantaḥ śātravāṃs tava
english: His warriors, O lord of kings, in armor and arms of many colors, will range through the battle, striking down your enemies.

sanskrit: vṛṣaseno rathāgryas te karṇaputro mahārathaḥ pradhakṣyati ripūṇāṃ te balāni balināṃ varaḥ
english: Vṛṣasena, foremost of your chariot-warriors, son of Karṇa and a great chariot-warrior, best of the mighty, will burn up the forces of your foes.

sanskrit: jalasaṃdho mahātejā rājan rathavaras tava tyakṣyate samare prāṇān māgadhaḥ paravīrahā
english: Jalasaṃdha of great splendor, O king, your foremost chariot-warrior, the Māgadha, slayer of enemy heroes, will yield up his life in battle.

sanskrit: eṣa yotsyati saṃgrāme gajaskandhaviśāradaḥ rathena vā mahābāhuḥ kṣapayañ śatruvāhinīm
english: He will fight in the battle, skilled upon the shoulders of an elephant, or by chariot — that mighty-armed one, wasting away the enemy host.

sanskrit: ratha eṣa mahārāja mato mama nararṣabhaḥ tvadarthe tyakṣyati prāṇān saha sainyo mahāraṇe
english: This chariot-warrior, O great king, I count a bull among men; in your cause he will lay down his life, together with his troops, in the great battle.

sanskrit: eṣa vikrāntayodhī ca citrayodhī ca saṃgare vītabhīś cāpi te rājañ śātravaiḥ saha yotsyate
english: He fights with valor and with cunning craft in the fray, and free of fear, O king, he will do battle with your enemies.

sanskrit: bāhlīko 'tirathaś caiva samare cānivartitā mama rājan mato yuddhe śūro vaivasvatopamaḥ
english: Bāhlika too is a great chariot-warrior and one who never turns back in battle; in the fight, O king, I count him a hero, the equal of Yama, son of the Sun.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa samaraṃ prāpya nivarteta kathaṃ cana yathā satatago rājan nābhihatya parān raṇe
english: For once he has reached the battle he would in no way turn back, O king, any more than the ever-moving wind, until he has struck down his foes in the fray.

sanskrit: senāpatir mahārāja satyavāṃs te mahārathaḥ raṇeṣv adbhutakarmā ca rathaḥ pararathārujaḥ
english: Your commander Satyavat, O great king, a great chariot-warrior, of wondrous deeds in battle, is a chariot-warrior who breaks the cars of his enemies.

sanskrit: etasya samaraṃ dṛṣṭvā na vyathāsti kathaṃ cana utsmayann abhyupaity eṣa parān rathapathe sthitān
english: Beholding battle, there is in him no faltering whatever; smiling, he advances upon the foes who stand in his chariot's path.

sanskrit: eṣa cāriṣu vikrāntaḥ karma satpuruṣocitam kartā vimarde sumahat tvadarthe puruṣottamaḥ
english: Valiant against his enemies, this best of men will do, in the crush of battle, a very great deed worthy of the noble, in your cause.

sanskrit: alāyudho rākṣasendraḥ krūrakarmā mahābalaḥ haniṣyati parān rājan pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: Alāyudha, lord of the rākṣasas, cruel in deed and of great might, will slay your foes, O king, remembering the enmity of old.

sanskrit: eṣa rākṣasasainyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ rathasattamaḥ māyāvī dṛḍhavairaś ca samare vicariṣyati
english: He, foremost chariot-warrior of all the rākṣasa hosts, a master of illusion and firm in his hatred, will range through the battle.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣādhipo vīro bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān gajāṅkuśadharaśreṣṭho rathe caiva viśāradaḥ
english: Bhagadatta, lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, a valorous and mighty hero, foremost among wielders of the elephant-goad and skilled also upon the chariot —

sanskrit: etena yuddham abhavat purā gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ divasān subahūn rājann ubhayor jayagṛddhinoḥ
english: With him the wielder of Gāṇḍīva once did battle for very many days, O king, both of them greedy for victory.

sanskrit: tataḥ sakhāyaṃ gāndhāre mānayan pākaśāsanam akarot saṃvidaṃ tena pāṇḍavena mahātmanā
english: Then, O Gāndhāra, honoring the chastiser of Pāka as his friend, he made a compact with that great-souled son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: eṣa yotsyati saṃgrāme gajaskandhaviśāradaḥ airāvatagato rājā devānām iva vāsavaḥ
english: He will fight in the battle, skilled upon the shoulders of his elephant, that king mounted as Vāsava mounted upon Airāvata among the gods.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca acalo vṛṣakaś caiva bhrātarau sahitāv ubhau rathau tava durādharṣau śatrūn vidhvaṃsayiṣyataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Acala and Vṛṣaka, two brothers united, are chariot-warriors of yours hard to assail; they will shatter your enemies.

sanskrit: balavantau naravyāghrau dṛḍhakrodhau prahāriṇau gāndhāramukhyau taruṇau darśanīyau mahābalau
english: Mighty tigers among men, firm in their wrath, strikers in battle, chiefs of the Gāndhāras, young, handsome, and of great strength.

sanskrit: sakhā te dayito nityaṃ ya eṣa raṇakarkaśaḥ protsāhayati rājaṃs tvāṃ vigrahe pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Your ever-beloved friend, hardened to war, who incites you, O king, to the quarrel with the Pāṇḍavas —

sanskrit: paruṣaḥ katthano nīcaḥ karṇo vaikartanas tava mantrī netā ca bandhuś ca mānī cātyantam ucchritaḥ
english: — harsh, boastful, base, your Karṇa Vaikartana, your counselor, leader, and kinsman, proud and exceedingly puffed up.

sanskrit: eṣa naiva rathaḥ pūrṇo nāpy evātiratho nṛpa viyuktaḥ kavacenaiṣa sahajena vicetanaḥ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca divyābhyāṃ viyuktaḥ satataṃ ghṛṇī
english: He is neither a full chariot-warrior nor a great chariot-warrior, O king; parted from the armor born with him, witless, and parted too from his two celestial earrings, he is ever soft of heart.

sanskrit: abhiśāpāc ca rāmasya brāhmaṇasya ca bhāṣaṇāt karaṇānāṃ viyogāc ca tena me 'rdharatho mataḥ naiṣa phalgunam āsādya punar jīvan vimokṣyate
english: By the curse of Rāma, by the word of a brāhmaṇa, and by the loss of his accoutrements, I therefore count him but half a chariot-warrior; once he meets Phalguna, he will not escape again alive.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato 'bravīn mahābāhur droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ evam etad yathāttha tvaṃ na mithyāstīti kiṃ cana
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the mighty-armed Droṇa, best of weapon-bearers, spoke: "It is just as you have said; there is not a word of falsehood in it."

sanskrit: raṇe raṇe 'timānī ca vimukhaś caiva dṛśyate ghṛṇī karṇaḥ pramādī ca tena me 'rdharatho mataḥ
english: "In battle after battle he is seen overproud and turning away from the fight; soft-hearted and heedless is Karṇa, and therefore I too count him but half a chariot-warrior."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu rādheyaḥ krodhād utphullalocanaḥ uvāca bhīṣmaṃ rājendra tudan vāgbhiḥ pratodavat
english: Hearing this, the son of Rādhā, his eyes wide with anger, O lord of kings, spoke to Bhīṣma, goading him with words as with a whip.

sanskrit: pitāmaha yatheṣṭaṃ māṃ vākśarair upakṛntasi anāgasaṃ sadā dveṣād evam eva pade pade marṣayāmi ca tat sarvaṃ duryodhanakṛtena vai
english: "Grandsire, you cut me at your pleasure with arrows of speech, though I am guiltless, ever out of hatred, at every step thus; yet I bear it all, every bit of it, for Duryodhana's sake."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu māṃ manyase 'śaktaṃ yathā kāpuruṣaṃ tathā bhavān ardharatho mahyaṃ mato nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: "But you deem me unfit, as though I were a coward; in my eyes it is you who are but half a chariot-warrior — of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: sarvasya jagataś caiva gāṅgeya na mṛṣā vade kurūṇām ahito nityaṃ na ca rājāvabudhyate
english: "I speak no falsehood before all the world, O son of Gaṅgā: you are forever the enemy of the Kurus, and the king does not perceive it."

sanskrit: ko hi nāma samāneṣu rājasūdāttakarmasu tejovadham imaṃ kuryād vibhedayiṣur āhave yathā tvaṃ guṇanirdeśād aparādhaṃ cikīrṣasi
english: "For who indeed, among kings equal and lofty in deed, would wreak such a slaying of another's spirit, eager to sow division before the battle, as you, under the guise of naming our qualities, seek to do us wrong?"

sanskrit: na hāyanair na palitair na vittair na ca bandhubhiḥ mahārathatvaṃ saṃkhyātuṃ śakyaṃ kṣatrasya kaurava
english: "Not by years, not by gray hairs, not by wealth, nor by kinsmen can the rank of a great chariot-warrior of the kṣatriya be reckoned, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: balajyeṣṭhaṃ smṛtaṃ kṣatraṃ mantrajyeṣṭhā dvijātayaḥ dhanajyeṣṭhāḥ smṛtā vaiśyāḥ śūdrās tu vayasādhikāḥ
english: "The kṣatriya is held to rank by strength, the twice-born by their counsel, the vaiśyas are reckoned by their wealth, but the śūdras by seniority of age."

sanskrit: yathecchakaṃ svayaṃgrāhād rathān atirathāṃs tathā kāmadveṣasamāyukto mohāt prakurute bhavān
english: "At your own whim and by your own arbitrary grasp you make out chariot-warriors and great chariot-warriors thus, swayed by desire and hatred, out of delusion."

sanskrit: duryodhana mahābāho sādhu samyag avekṣyatām tyajyatāṃ duṣṭabhāvo 'yaṃ bhīṣmaḥ kilbiṣakṛt tava
english: "O mighty-armed Duryodhana, let it be well and rightly considered; let this Bhīṣma of evil disposition be cast off, who works your harm."

sanskrit: bhinnā hi senā nṛpate duḥsaṃdheyā bhavaty uta maulāpi puruṣavyāghra kim u nānā samutthitā
english: "For an army once divided, O king, becomes hard to reunite — even one of hereditary loyalty, O tiger among men; how much more one raised from sundry sources?"
